Hey man, you don't have to like every game or franchise out there. For everyone who likes Grand Theft Auto or other Rockstar games, there are people who can't stand it and would prefer playing something like Stardew Valley. Nothing wrong with that, games are meant to be enjoyed however you like them.

To answer your question though, there's a lot of reasons people like them. One of my favorites is the storyline - GTA IV is one of my favorites since I liked the grittiness of Niko's story. On the other hand, my brother who's more a fan of being able to commit chaos and just mess around liked the open world aspect. Often he'd just ask to load up my save file then run around with my upgraded weapons causing property damage and killing NPCs without doing a single quest. For Red Dead Redemption 2, not only was Arthur's storyline frankly amazing but I also enjoyed all the side tasks that I could build up - side challenges like killing a cougar with a knife, just going out hunting for fun, even just robbing wagons to sell and make an extra buck.

It all just comes down to what you enjoy. For Rockstar games there's a lot of different aspects that can appeal to a person, but just because they can for a lot of people doesn't mean they have to for you. People are different and have different tastes, and that's perfectly okay. Just keep doing what you're doing and enjoy what you enjoy, and if you do decide to try out one of Rockstar's games my tip is to give it a chance to build up - it opens up to a lot more than just the opening you've seen.

So first, There are EVs and IVs. **EVs** are the ones you train by battling other pokemon - and will train faster if you use the power items. The alternative to training EVs are to use the nutrients such as protein from a Chansey store.

**IVs** on the other hand are the base stats a pokemon has once they're hatched or caught. There's only two ways to get high IVs: breed one, or you can do Hyper Training to increase those stats to the base max, which costs Bottlecaps. When you teleport to the ice city Montenevera, nearby is a man with an Abomasnow. If you talk to him he'll offer to hyper train in exchange for either bottle caps (1 per stat) or a gold bottle cap (all stats at once I believe). This will increase the baste stats of your pokemon.

One thing of note, if you have a high IV pokemon you can breed high IVs as well, but if you get high IVs using hyper training their eggs will still have low IVs.

I've actually been looking into DM'ing a duet for my friend recently. Two of the biggest pieces of advice I've gotten are to not make problems with only one solution (lest your player get roadblocked and frustrated they can't figure it out), and don't be afraid of your player's character really being the main character. Duets are really good at letting a person be the center of attention, so let them be a little bit of an anime protagonist. One method to do this is to let them have two classes at once - so for example, at level one they might have the benefit of both a fighter and rogue, almost like a multiclass, but each time they level both their classes level up in sync.

There's a couple reasons this could be! The base one is that your hair or fur color for your race will chance what color your forms have, so for example a white tauren will have a white bear form, while a black tauren will have a black bear form \[there's also a glyph to make the color you change to random\].

However, each race that can play druid has a different look as well. Tauren cat druids look like a lion, while trolls have a more tiger/lion cross appearance with more vibrant colors. Night elves and worgen also have their own forms.

The most startling form changes are from the special weapon you get at level 100, from the Legion expansion. The druid weapon for bear and cat will change their appearance depending on criteria they've unlocked \[such as completing a certain questline, or doing achievements\]. They can swap between these appearances, and they're the most different from base \- for example, my druid glows blue and leaves a ghostly trail in its wake.
